d: The Compliance Officer is responsible for establishing, administering and maintaining BloFin’s compliance management system (“CMS”), so that BloFin complies at all times with its VARA licence conditions, the VARA Regulations, Rules and Directives, the Federal AML-CFT Laws and all other applicable UAE laws, the applicable laws of any other jurisdiction in which BloFin carries out VA Activities or similar business, and its own constitutional documents and internal policies.

The CO is accountable for identifying and escalating material non-compliance, notifying VARA and other relevant authorities where required, and embedding a professional compliance culture across the Board, Senior Management and Staff.

VARA requires every VASP to appoint a Compliance Officer who possesses at least five (5) years of relevant experience in a compliance function, is a Fit and Proper Person as approved by VARA, is resident in the UAE or holds a UAE passport, is a full-time employee of the VASP and reports directly to the Board. The appointment must be reviewed annually to confirm the CO remains Fit and Proper. The CO is ultimately responsible for establishing and administering the CMS and for notifying VARA and other relevant authorities of any material non-compliance by the VASP, its Board or its Staff. Compliance activities may be delegated to appropriate professionals, provided the CO remains accountable and VARA’s outsourcing requirements are met. As head of the compliance function, the CO is treated as a member of Senior Management and may not hold a position on the Board.

The CO reports directly to the Board of Directors and attends the Compliance Committee where one is established. The CMS must be independent of all operational and business functions, and the compliance function must be segregated from and independent of the operational and related supervisory functions. The CO may liaise with the CEO on administrative matters only; this does not create a reporting line and does not restrict the CO’s direct and unrestricted access to the Board. The CO works alongside the MLRO, the Head of Risk, the CISO / DPO, the Responsible Individuals, the Company Secretary and the internal and external auditors.
r: Establish, administer and maintain an effective CMS that covers all relevant aspects of BloFin’s operations, including unfettered access by the Board and relevant Staff to necessary records and documentation.
Ensure the CMS is independent of all operational and business functions, and that the CO is notified promptly of any material non-compliance.
Ensure the compliance function has the technical competence, financial and non-financial resources and experience necessary to perform its functions.

Design and run a risk-based compliance testing and monitoring programme that regularly selects and reviews different areas of the business and analyses key performance and risk indicators, to identify potential compliance violations.
Review and update the CMS and compliance policies and procedures from time to time so they remain aligned with BloFin’s business and the changing regulatory landscape.

Develop and implement clear and detailed compliance policies and procedures that enable all Staff and the Board to comply with all applicable legal and regulatory requirements, including licence conditions, record keeping, business practices, AML/CFT, and client, proprietary and Staff dealing requirements.

Ensure the policies provide for client complaints to be handled properly, with appropriate remedial action, and investigated by Staff who are not directly involved in the subject matter of the complaint.

Develop and implement compliance policies and procedures, including the Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan (“BCDR Plan”) required under the Technology and Information Rulebook, working with the CISO, COO and Head of Risk.
Notify VARA and other relevant authorities of any material non-compliance by BloFin, its Board or its Staff with applicable legal and regulatory requirements.
Ensure a report is submitted to VARA immediately upon discovery of any violation or breach of any law, Regulation, Rule or Directive related to the conduct of any VA Activity.

Ensure VARA is notified in writing of any changes to the items in BloFin’s annual regulatory submission, and immediately of any criminal or material civil action, Insolvency Proceeding, investigation, inspection or enquiry against BloFin, its Board members, UBOs or Senior Management.
Coordinate with the CISO so that material cybersecurity events, and events triggering the BCDR Plan that materially impact operations, are reported to VARA within seventy-two (72) hours of detection.
Ensure information on BloFin’s activities in jurisdictions other than the Emirate is disclosed to VARA on request.

Act as a primary point of contact for VARA on compliance matters, dealing with VARA in an open and transparent manner, and coordinate timely, accurate responses to VARA requests, RFIs, supervisory queries and inspections.
Coordinate and oversee the completeness and timeliness of BloFin’s monthly, quarterly and annual regulatory submissions to VARA, working with the CFO, Head of Risk and Company Secretary.

Ensure quarterly submissions include the minutes of all Board and Board committee meetings, the statement of compliance with financial requirements, financial projections and strategic business plans, and the Head of Risk’s risk exposure report.
Coordinate the annual assessment by Senior Management of BloFin’s compliance with applicable laws, Regulations, Rules and Directives for the fiscal year.

Ensure Staff, including Senior Management, are properly and adequately trained in their understanding of and compliance with all applicable laws and regulatory requirements, including those relating to consumer protection and AML/CFT.

Ensure operational policies and procedures are communicated to new hires within their first thirty (30) calendar days, and that updated policies are promptly communicated and made available to all Staff.
Ensure all Staff performing compliance functions are Fit and Proper Persons and possess the necessary skills, qualifications and experience for their roles.
Compliance Risk, Board Reporting and Corrective Action
Assess emerging compliance issues and risks, and provide input to the Head of Risk on compliance-function and regulatory risks for the quarterly risk exposure report.
Report compliance activities and compliance audits to the Board.

Where necessary, ensure appropriate corrective actions are taken in response to deficiencies in the CMS or non-compliance with any applicable laws or regulatory requirements, and track them to closure.
Act as BloFin’s internal counterpart to the MLRO, ensuring the MLRO has timely access to the information, systems and Staff needed to discharge the MLRO’s duties.
Receive immediate notification from the MLRO when a Suspicious Transaction report has been made, provided this does not constitute tipping-off.
Monitor that the MLRO arrangement continues to meet the management requirements of the Company Rulebook, and escalate any concerns to the Board.
Hold primary and day-to-day responsibility for implementing BloFin’s anti-bribery and corruption policy and monitoring its effectiveness, addressing any deficiencies as soon as possible.

Receive reports from the Board or Staff of actual, suspected or solicited breaches; prepare a written summary of any oral report; and investigate each report by appointing an independent Entity to commission the investigation.
Handle all reports, including those from outside BloFin, confidentially, protecting the identity of the person reporting in accordance with applicable UAE law.
Advise the Board of the existence of any investigation and of any finding of unlawful conduct, and ensure any such finding is reported to VARA immediately.
Retain investigation reports and remediation summaries for no less than eight (8) years from completion of the remedial action, and make them available to VARA on request.

Where compliance activities are delegated to appropriate professionals, remain accountable for the implementation of the CMS and ensure all applicable Company Rulebook requirements, including outsourcing management requirements, are met.

Administer BloFin’s conflicts of interest policy and the conflicts of interest register, and BloFin’s personal dealing procedures, including prior written approval of Board and Staff dealings in Virtual Assets and six-monthly position notifications.
Ensure compliance records are retained for no less than eight (8) years, or indefinitely where records may relate to the national security of the UAE.

q: A minimum of two years' experience as a CDP Pastry in an upscale hotel, resort, cruise ship or convention banqueting service (shipboard experience preferred).
Very strong management skills in a multicultural and dynamic environment.
Very strong communication, problem solving, decision making, and interpersonal skills.
Superior customer service, teambuilding, and conflict resolution skills.

Knowledge of the principles and processes for providing personalized services including needs assessment techniques, quality service standards, alternative delivery systems, and guest satisfaction evaluation techniques.
Strong planning, coaching, organizing, staffing, controlling, and evaluating skills.
Possess a good understanding of basic accounting principles such as numbering flow, “Debits/Credits”, adjusting entries and corrections.
Ability to write reports and business correspondence and to establish a good rapport with the ship’s Senior Officers and the corporate office.
r: Ensures the smooth and efficient operation and control of the pastry galley and production daily according to company policies.
Directs, coaches, supports, supervises, and evaluates (with the Assistant Pastry Chef) the performance of all direct reports.
Responsible for the production, quality and presentation of the pastry and dessert assortment to be used in the daily menus.
Prepares production forecasts and records leftovers to avoid unnecessary wastage and keep food costs within the budget.
Supervise the set-up of the Pastry and dessert display in the various buffets.
Must have a complete knowledge of the United States Public Health rules and regulations and ensure that they are followed daily.

Ensures that the Pastry Shop’s cleaning schedule established by the Executive Sous Chef Pastry & Bakery is followed by all team members on duty after each service and exercises proper methods to minimize equipment damages.
Ensures that the pantry shops are ready for any announced or unannounced USPH inspections done either by the ship’s management or USPH inspectors.
Responsible for the requisition and transportation of the necessary items from the main stores to the pastry galley.
Ensures recipes/master list and yields are in accordance with the company’s standards.
Assists the Assistant Pastry Chef with completing the daily pastry consumption re-cap as requested by the Executive Chef.

Ensures that Pastry team members come to work on time, and are in proper, well-maintained uniforms, with special attention to those working in public areas. Personal appearance and hygiene must be according to company policy.
Has a thorough understanding of Time and Attendance procedures and is familiar with the contracts and work schedule hours/week and supporting documentation.
Is aware of and/or acquires the necessary knowledge to comply with the ship’s standard operation, to assist guests and crew members with inquiries.
Attends meetings, training activities, courses and all other work-related activities as required.
Accountable to coach and train the Pastry Cooks.
Performs related duties as required. This position description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the shipboard employee occupying this position.
Shipboard employees will be required to perform any other job-related duties assigned by their supervisor or management.
